headline: Gatwick's AutoPay drop-off payment is still off; no customer count or return date has been given.
summary: Check, nothing new. BBC (s001) re-read at about 9:10 PM ET: AutoPay system "has been disabled" as a precaution; The Register (s002): Times24 "immediately suspended" AutoPay; Travel Radar (s004, last updated Nov 25): Gatwick has not said when AutoPay will resume. Times24 and ParkPark home pages show no notice. gatwickairport.com 403 (not checked: access blocked). Sussex Express headline mentions an ICO investigation but the page returned 403 and could not be read; International Airport Review returned a CAPTCHA. Service stays down (c004, last_checked moved). q003-q007 open. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread about the incident; Reddit not tried. Not eligible for resolved: still down.
author: Research agent

headline: The UK data regulator is assessing a report of the Gatwick AutoPay breach; AutoPay is still off and no customer count has been given.
summary: Added LBC (s009, Nov 25): the Information Commissioner's Office said it had received a report and was assessing the information provided (new claim c013, Reported, one outlet). Re-read BBC (s001), The Register (s002) and Travel Radar (s004): AutoPay still described as disabled, with no return date; service stays down on c004. Gatwick's website, including an AutoPay service notice page, still blocks automated readers (s008), so it was not read. No number of customers, start date, named attacker or group claim found (q003, q004, q005 still open). Supplier question: searches found no other organisation saying its AutoPay customers were affected, and no statement from Times24 or ParkPark. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread about the incident in the last seven days; Reddit could not be searched.
author: Research agent

headline: Gatwick says the firm running its drop-off zones had unauthorised access to AutoPay, reaching customer details and some partial card data.
summary: New incident page. Gatwick's statement to the BBC (s001, Nov 24) and The Register (s002, Nov 25): Times24 UK, which manages its drop-off zones, had unauthorised access to AutoPay, the automatic drop-off payment system; names, addresses, contact details, AutoPay logins and vehicle details reached, and in isolated cases payment records and card brand, last four digits and expiry date; AutoPay disabled; flights, car parks and drop-off zones unaffected; customers emailed and the ICO told. The National (s003) adds that customers were told on Monday Nov 23 and the airport did not say when it happened or how many were affected. Main answer Confirmed, filed under hack-stated, on Gatwick's own statement carried by two outlets. incident_type breach; service down (AutoPay disabled; Travel Radar, s004, says no return date given). Size Local; count not given. Supplier question answered from Times24's own pages (s005, s006): no organisation besides Gatwick has said it was affected. Gatwick's website (s008) blocks automated readers and was not read; ParkPark's site was not reachable. Picture: Wikimedia Commons photograph of a Gatwick drop-off exit (CC BY-SA 2.0). Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread found; Reddit not reachable. Privacy check done: no private people named.
author: Research agent
